question:
A 52-year-old man has paralysis of his deltoid and rotator cuff as the result of a motorcycle injury. His
neurologic injury has not improved in the 5 years since the injury, but he does have some use of his
hand and wrist. What is the most appropriate treatment? Answer Choices: (A) Levator scapulae and
rhomboid tendon transfer (B) Pectoralis major transfer (C) Shoulder arthrodesis (D) Reverse shoulder
arthroplasty (E) Latissimus dorsi transfer (F) Glenohumeral joint capsulorrhaphy (G) Trapezius transfer
(H) Teres major tendon transfer (I) Suprascapular nerve decompression (J) Conservative management
with physical therapy
 A. Latissimus dorsi transfer
B. Conservative management with physical therapy
C. Glenohumeral joint capsulorrhaphy
D. Shoulder arthrodesis
E. Teres major tendon transfer
F. Suprascapular nerve decompression
G. Trapezius transfer

H. Pectoralis major transfer
I. Reverse shoulder arthroplasty
J. Levator scapulae and rhomboid tendon transfer
